themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline of 1.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 146% increase (z-score: 3.41)—suggesting either a localized environmental event or emerging pollution source affecting Central Harlem residents this week.
evidence: Air quality complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (146% spike, z-score: 3.41)
Signal emerged abruptly this week with no prior escalation pattern
Timing aligns with potential seasonal or industrial activity change
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: interview residents about air quality symptoms and identify any visible pollution sources, construction, or traffic patterns that changed this week
City agency outreach: contact DEP and DOHMH to determine if they've detected air quality anomalies in CD 110 or nearby industrial/transit corridors

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks jumped to 8 last week versus a baseline of 0.9 per week—an 814% spike (z-score: 6.11)—indicating a sudden and significant disruption to park use, potentially tied to events, music venues, or unregulated amplified sound.
evidence: Park noise complaints: 8 last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (814% spike, z-score: 6.11)
Sharp one-week spike suggests acute event rather than chronic problem
Spike predates this week but remains the second-most recent major anomaly
reporting_angles: Identify which parks (Marcus Garvey, Mt. Morris, etc.) received complaints and what events or activities coincided with last week's spike
Interview NYPD and Parks Enforcement Patrol about noise enforcement response and whether there are recurring events driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Garbage Disposal & Sanitation Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 7 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.4 per week—a 195% increase (z-score: 3.8)—alongside elevated requests for litter baskets (1233% spike, 5 complaints vs. 0.4 avg), signaling a garbage collection or street sanitation crisis in the district.
evidence: Residential disposal complaints: 7 (two weeks ago) vs. 2.4 weekly average (195% spike, z-score: 3.8)
Litter basket requests: 5 (two weeks ago) vs. 0.4 weekly average (1233% spike, z-score: 9.55—highest severity)
Convergence of two disposal-related complaint types suggests systemic collection or infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: DSNY investigation: verify whether there were collection delays, missed pickups, or staffing shortages in CD 110 two weeks ago and whether service has normalized
Street reporting: document conditions at high-complaint areas and interview residents about persistence of garbage pileup; check if litter basket density is actually inadequate

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints surged to 27 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 8.2 per week—a 227% spike (z-score: 4.1)—suggesting either a specific traffic event, enforcement gap, or emerging illegal street racing activity in Central Harlem.
evidence: Vehicle noise complaints: 27 (two weeks ago) vs. 8.2 weekly average (227% spike, z-score: 4.1)
Spike is specific to vehicle noise (not general noise), narrowing potential causes
Timing coincides with potential start of warmer weather and increased outdoor activity
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Traffic Enforcement about any traffic incidents, street racing patterns, or enforcement operations in CD 110 two weeks ago
Community reporting: identify which corridors (major avenues, highways bordering district) experienced worst congestion or illegal vehicle activity

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about dead or dying trees hit 3 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 4.16)—indicating potential tree disease, environmental stress, or deferred maintenance in parks and street medians that warrants Parks Department investigation.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 3 (two weeks ago) vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
Concentrated spike suggests localized issue (disease, drought, vandalism) rather than gradual decline
Community board budget includes repeated requests for facility upgrades and tree/greenspace management
reporting_angles: Parks Department interview: determine if there's a known tree disease outbreak in CD 110 or if recent weather stressed street trees
Ground reporting: locate and photograph the affected trees, assess their condition and proximity to residents
